feedback.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{8{e}^{-2s}}{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{u}_{2}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s},\,s>0,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${u}_{2}(t)=u(t-2)$ is the unit step function.

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{u}_{2}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{u}_{2}(t)}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s}} \\ {u}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s}} & ={u}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-2s}}{s}}=8\cdot {u}_{2}(t) \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{8{e}^{-2s}}{s}}=8{u}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$
